\section{Text cleaning and language split}

\begin{itemize}
  \item Detector: \texttt{lingua}, 20 languages common in K-pop comments, picked by hand (\texttt{common.LANGUAGES}).
  \item Why not all 75: short English comments came out as Sotho or Tswana.
  \item Flow: Figure~\ref{fig:lang_flow}.
\end{itemize}

Two versions per video:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{English:} the first \nEnVideoA{} English comments.
  \item \textbf{Mixed:} all fetched comments, every language.
\end{itemize}

\clearpage

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.03\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.33\linewidth}@{}}
  \toprule
  \# & Step & What it does & Why \\
  \midrule
  1 & Language & Detect language first. & Gives the English version. \\
  \midrule
  2 & Lowercase & All letters lowercase. & As \texttt{tm}. \\
  \midrule
  3 & Drop symbols & Drop punctuation, numbers, emoji. Keep every script. & As \texttt{tm}. No cloud font draws emoji. \\
  \midrule
  4 & Stopwords & Drop \texttt{tm} English stopwords. & As \texttt{tm}. English only. \\
  \midrule
  5 & Short words & Drop words under 3 letters. & \texttt{tm} default \texttt{wordLengths = c(3, Inf)}. \\
  \midrule
  6 & No stemming & Keep full words. & The R script loads \texttt{SnowballC} but never calls it. \\
  \midrule
  7 & Cloud & Top 150 words, fixed seed. & Same cloud on every run. \\
  \bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Cleaning steps from comment to terms.}\label{tab:cleaning}
\end{table}

\begin{itemize}
  \item No stemming: many stems are not dictionary words (\texttt{army} $\to$ \texttt{armi}, \texttt{happy} $\to$ \texttt{happi}).
  \item 3-letter minimum: with 2, Spanish and Portuguese words (\texttt{de}, \texttt{la}, \texttt{en}) enter the clouds.
\end{itemize}

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

% Owner's words, verbatim: discussion_owner.md (2026-10-07). Translated; data checks noted there.
Both are Korean K-pop groups: \vidA{} by a boy group, \vidB{} by a girl group.

\textbf{Before the analysis: what I expected}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Both have large global fandoms, so many comments in English and other languages, not only Korean.
  \item Frequent words: group name, song, member names, ``love'', fandom name.
  \item One better-known member gets more mentions.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{After: common to both}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Group name, ``love'', fandom name and song are in the top 10 (Tables~\ref{tab:top_en} and~\ref{tab:top_mixed}).
  \item As expected, member names rank high, mostly in the top 30 (Lisa 4th in BLACKPINK mixed).
  \item Pride in views and fame: \texttt{views}, \texttt{billion}.
  \item Fandom names: \texttt{army} (BTS), \texttt{blinks} (BLACKPINK).
  \item The mixed comments hold many languages: a global audience.
  \item \texttt{anyone}: the videos are 6 (BTS) and 7 (BLACKPINK) years old. Returning fans ask others who is still watching (``September 2026 anyone?''). Many old fans keep coming back.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{After: boy group vs.\ girl group}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Words show boy vs.\ girl group: \texttt{boys}, \texttt{kings} only in the BTS cloud, \texttt{girls}, \texttt{queens} only in the BLACKPINK cloud.
  \item BTS fans comment far more. Views are close, but comments per 1,000 views are about 7 times higher (Table~\ref{tab:engagement}).
  \item BTS: \texttt{comments}. Fans seem proud of the video's comment count.
  \item BTS: \texttt{fighting} (the Korean cheer) appears.
  \item BTS: all members finished military service and tour together again. \texttt{comeback} appears, but rarely.
  \item BTS: recent comments (2026-10-03 and 10-04) reflect the tour's concert in Bogotá, Colombia.
  \item BTS: one better-known member holds true. Only Jungkook and Jimin are in the English cloud (2 of 7).
  \item BLACKPINK: all 4 members are in both clouds. Lisa leads only in mixed.
  \item BLACKPINK: \texttt{anniversary} stands out: the group's 10th anniversary, mostly in the newest comments.
  \item BLACKPINK: fans miss the group (\texttt{miss}). The members left one agency for their own and work solo.
  \item BLACKPINK: the fan chant ``BLACKPINK in your area'' (\texttt{area}).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{After: English vs.\ mixed}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{que} (``that'') and \texttt{amo} (``I love''), Spanish and Portuguese, appear in both mixed clouds (Table~\ref{tab:shared}): both have Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking fans, more for BTS.
  \item BLACKPINK: Thai comments appear, Lisa's home country. BTS has none.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Conclusion}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Both have global fandoms, and old fans keep coming back.
  \item BTS: the tour shows in recent comments (Bogotá concert). Spanish comments are many, but not more recently.
  \item BLACKPINK: recent comments center on members and its 10th anniversary.
\end{itemize}
